item.title: ‘India is the second largest market for Claude, developers here doing the most intense work’: As India hosts AI Impact Summit, global giant Anthropic opens office
item.description: Anthropic has officially opened its Bengaluru office, marking India as its second-largest global market. Led by Irina Ghose, the expansion includes major partnerships in aviation, education, and agriculture, alongside a dedicated push to improve AI performance in ten widely spoken Indian languages.

item.title: Muhammad Yunus and the ‘seven sisters’ dog whistle: How Bangladesh’s outgoing chief rekindled tensions with India and whitewashed attacks on Hindus
item.description: Muhammad Yunus exited office not with introspection, but with a geopolitical provocation aimed at India’s Northeast and a convenient silence on minority persecution.

item.title: 1 year of the BJP govt in Delhi: A governance shift from AAP’s subsidy politics to structural development
item.description: Long-term infrastructure modernisation plans worth approximately ₹17,000 crore include underground cable expansion, grid strengthening, and installation of modern monitoring systems. The objective is to improve reliability, safety, and the quality of urban infrastructure by reducing reliance on overhead power distribution.

item.title: Tribal villages can bar entry of missionaries: Read how SC rejected Colin Gonsalves’ plea and upheld Chhattisgarh HC’s stand amid rampant forced conversions
item.description: According to the Solicitor General, the high court had directed the petitioners to get in touch with the Gram Sabhas.

item.title: Galgotias University plays victim card, claims ‘negative propaganda’ after Chinese robot dog fiasco: Read how they are lying
item.description: After criticism erupted, the university denied ever claiming ownership. However, televised remarks, a rebranded ORION showcase, and government handle amplification suggest the Chinese robot was projected as an in house AI achievement.

item.title: 18 crore devotees, 1.2 lakh jobs, over 400 crores in tax revenue: Read how Ram Mandir is transforming Ayodhya into a global pilgrimage site, changing people’s lives
item.description: The Ram Mandir paid taxes to the government of about ₹400 crore between 5th February of 2020 and 2025.

item.title: NGT clears the Great Nicobar Project: Read how Congress has been opposing the mega project crucial for India
item.description: The National Green Tribunal has cleared the ₹90,000-crore Great Nicobar project, citing its strategic importance in countering China.

item.title: ‘Savarna marriages and movements are inherently narcissistic and anti democratic’: Meet the Ambedkarite dean at Galgotias casting an entire community as flawed
item.description: As Dean at Galgotias University, Kisana authored essays on weddings, dating, humour and MBA culture, repeatedly attributing structural and psychological flaws to Savarnas while framing opposition to UGC regulations as reactionary backlash.

item.title: India’s highways go green: NHAI launches Bee Corridors to support pollinators and boost rural economy
item.description: NHAI’s ‘Bee Corridors’ plan will transform India’s highways into pollinator-friendly green arteries, linking infrastructure growth with PM Modi’s Sweet Revolution and biodiversity goals.

item.title: The Purvanchal Expressway turnaround under Yogi: How the UP govt saved Rs 3,400 crore by scrapping illegal tenders issued by Akhilesh Yadav’s SP
item.description: The Purvanchal Expressway remains one of the flagship infrastructure projects in the state. With more expressways under construction and new ones in the pipeline, the debate over development models is likely to remain at the centre of Uttar Pradesh’s political narrative.
